name: CDW product pages - published lead-time ranges for GPU and AI server SKUs (observed 2026-10-04)
notes: CDW is, as of this access, one of very few enterprise distributors that PRINTS a lead time rather than routing to 'request a quote' - which makes it the most useful lead-time source available in this repo, and the basis for the only non-null lead_time_weeks values written here. Two fetch routes were used: the GPU-server search results page and the RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell search page. VERBATIM lead-time strings with their SKU, MFG # and CDW # as displayed on 2026-10-04. SCARCE / NEW-GENERATION DATACENTER PARTS, all showing '4-6+ Weeks': NVIDIA DGX B200 8X180GB Server with Full 3-Year Support (MFG DGXB-G1440+P2CMI36, CDW 8055598, also 'Request Pricing' i.e. no published price); NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96GB graphics card (MFG 900-2G153-0000-000, CDW 8379294, 'Request Pricing'); NVIDIA L4 Tensor Core 24GB GPU computing processor (S0K89C, CDW 7532302, $7,989.99). ALSO '4-6+ Weeks': QNAP TS-H3077AFU-R7-64G-US NAS and HPE P55094-B21 4-double-wide GPU FIO enablement kit for ProLiant DL385 Gen11 - both NON-GPU or infrastructure items carrying the same 4-6+ week window, which is the tell that the figure is CDW's inbound/distribution lead time as much as the part's own scarcity. SHORTER, IN STOCK-ADJACENT PARTS: NVIDIA A16 64GB GPU computing processor (R8T26C, CDW 7342826, $9,277.99) at '10-12+ Days'; NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition (MFG 900-2G147-0000-000, CDW 9077550) at '9-11+ Days'; ConnectX-7 at '1-3+ Days' (recorded 2026-10-03 in cdw-enterprise). BACKORDERED, NO WINDOW AT ALL - the honest negative: PNY/NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 96GB bare workstation cards (CDW 8326705 / 8326706 / 9039015), RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition full-height kit (NVRTXPRO6000TCGPU-KIT, CDW 8426124, $16,115.00) and NVIDIA DGX Spark (NVDGXSPARK-PB, CDW 8392823, $5,906.99) all read 'Item Backordered' with NO week estimate - so for the scarcest SKUs CDW publishes LESS than for the merely-constrained ones. READ THE '+' SIGNS: '4-6+ Weeks' is an open-ended range, not 4 to 6 weeks; and a distributor lead time measures THEIR inbound, so it is a lower bound on what a buyer faces and is not the OEM's build-and-ship time.
